instruction: How do I find the shortest path between two nodes in a Graphoid graph?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }
g.add_node("A", 1)
g.add_node("B", 2)
g.add_node("C", 3)
g.add_node("D", 4)
g.add_edge("A", "B", "road")
g.add_edge("B", "C", "road")
g.add_edge("A", "D", "highway")
g.add_edge("D", "C", "highway")

path = g.shortest_path("A", "C")
print(path)  # [A, B, C]

instruction: How do I check if a path exists between two nodes in Graphoid?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }
g.add_node("A", 1)
g.add_node("B", 2)
g.add_node("C", 3)
g.add_edge("A", "B", "link")
g.add_edge("B", "C", "link")

print(g.has_path("A", "C"))  # true
print(g.has_path("C", "A"))  # false (directed graph)

instruction: How do I find all paths between two nodes in a Graphoid graph?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }
g.add_node("A", 1)
g.add_node("B", 2)
g.add_node("C", 3)
g.add_node("D", 4)
g.add_edge("A", "B", "road")
g.add_edge("B", "C", "road")
g.add_edge("A", "D", "road")
g.add_edge("D", "C", "road")

# all_paths requires from, to, and max_length
paths = g.all_paths("A", "C", 5)
print(paths)  # [[A, B, C], [A, D, C]]

instruction: How do I get the distance between two nodes in a Graphoid graph?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }
g.add_node("A", 1)
g.add_node("B", 2)
g.add_node("C", 3)
g.add_edge("A", "B", "link")
g.add_edge("B", "C", "link")

# distance returns number of hops
print(g.distance("A", "C"))  # 2
print(g.distance("A", "B"))  # 1

instruction: How do I list all nodes and edges in a Graphoid graph?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }
g.add_node("server", "web-01")
g.add_node("db", "postgres-01")
g.add_node("cache", "redis-01")
g.add_edge("server", "db", "connects")
g.add_edge("server", "cache", "connects")

print(g.nodes())       # [server, db, cache]
print(g.edges())       # [[server, db, connects], [server, cache, connects]]
print(g.node_count())  # 3
print(g.edge_count())  # 2

instruction: How do I access and modify node values in a Graphoid graph?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }

# Add nodes with ID and value
g.add_node("alice", "Alice Smith")
g.add_node("bob", "Bob Jones")

# Read node value
print(g.get_node("alice"))  # Alice Smith
print(g["bob"])             # Bob Jones (index syntax)

# Set node value via index
g["charlie"] = "Charlie Brown"
print(g.node_count())  # 3

# Remove a node (also removes its edges)
g.remove_node("charlie")
print(g.node_count())  # 2

instruction: How do I check if a node exists in a Graphoid graph?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }
g.add_node("A", 1)
g.add_node("B", 2)

# Use has_node to check existence
print(g.has_node("A"))  # true
print(g.has_node("Z"))  # false

# You can also use index access — returns none for missing nodes
val = g["A"]
print(val)  # 1

instruction: How do I find shortest paths with edge type filtering in a Graphoid graph?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }
g.add_node("A", 1)
g.add_node("B", 2)
g.add_node("C", 3)
g.add_node("D", 4)
g.add_edge("A", "B", "road")
g.add_edge("B", "C", "road")
g.add_edge("A", "D", "highway")
g.add_edge("D", "C", "highway")

# Default shortest path (any edge type)
print(g.shortest_path("A", "C"))  # [A, B, C]

# Filter by edge type
print(g.shortest_path("A", "C", "highway"))  # [A, D, C]

instruction: How do I remove edges from a Graphoid graph?
output:
g = graph { type: :directed }
g.add_node("A", 1)
g.add_node("B", 2)
g.add_node("C", 3)
g.add_edge("A", "B", "link")
g.add_edge("B", "C", "link")
print(g.edge_count())  # 2

# remove_edge takes (from, to)
g.remove_edge("A", "B")
print(g.edge_count())  # 1
print(g.has_path("A", "C"))  # false — path broken

instruction: How do I create a DAG and enforce no-cycle constraints in Graphoid?
output:
# Use the :dag ruleset for directed acyclic graphs
dag = graph{}.with_ruleset(:dag)

dag.add_node("compile", 1)
dag.add_node("test", 2)
dag.add_node("deploy", 3)
dag.add_edge("compile", "test", "before")
dag.add_edge("test", "deploy", "before")

# Attempting to create a cycle will be rejected
try {
    dag.add_edge("deploy", "compile", "before")
} catch as e {
    print(e)  # Rule violation: no_cycles
}

print(dag.nodes())  # [compile, test, deploy]
